title: Add bounded tool calling to the structured llm package
objective: Extend the standalone llm package with versioned tool definitions, normalized tool calls, parallel tool call batches, optional automatic tool invocation, OpenRouter tool transport, and schema-validated tool-aware responses while preserving llm/request/v1 and llm/response/v1 behavior.

branch.name: wi-0001-llm-tool-calling
branch.rationale: The work item is implemented as a serial set of scoped commits on the current repository branch unless an operator creates a topic branch before delivery.

request.text: Review llm/* and add bounded tool calling. Support declaring available tools, invoking tools during an llm invocation, autoInvokeTools, parallel tool call batches represented as tool_calls, and common schemas for tool calls, parallel tool call batches, and the complete tool_calls array. A tool-round limit violation is an unvalidated response and must execute no tool calls. Design, implement, review, test, review, and commit each prepared work-item step.

scope.name: versioned-tool-contracts
scope.description: Add versioned request/response contracts and reusable schemas for tool definitions, tool calls, parallel tool call batches, tool results, and tool-aware output.
scope.reason: The existing v1 request and response objects are closed contracts and must remain backward compatible.

scope.name: provider-tool-transport
scope.description: Normalize provider-native tool declarations, tool calls, and tool results through an injected provider boundary and the OpenRouter adapter.
scope.reason: Provider wire formats must not leak into callers or tool-invocation policy.

scope.name: bounded-tool-orchestration
scope.description: Support manual pending tool calls and optional automatic invocation with sequential batches, parallel calls inside each batch, bounded rounds, bounded calls, abort handling, and fail-closed validation.
scope.reason: Tool execution must be deterministic, bounded, and safe when a model requests invalid or excessive work.

scope.name: offline-evidence
scope.description: Add provider-injected, mocked-transport, schema, typecheck, build, CLI, and documentation evidence without live provider calls or real tool execution.
scope.reason: The package must prove the public boundary without credentials or external side effects.

nonGoals.name: v1-contract-mutation
nonGoals.description: Do not add tool fields to llm/request/v1 or change llm/response/v1 semantics.
nonGoals.reason: Existing consumers depend on the closed v1 contracts.

nonGoals.name: unrestricted-execution
nonGoals.description: Do not discover tools, execute shell text, resolve arbitrary module paths, make network calls from the tool invoker, or persist tool results.
nonGoals.reason: The llm package declares and invokes only the caller-supplied in-memory ToolInvoker boundary.

nonGoals.name: downstream-agent-migration
nonGoals.description: Do not migrate Vector AgentWork, Cline compatibility, or other downstream consumers in this work item.
nonGoals.reason: This work item owns the reusable llm package boundary only.

items.name: preserve-v1
items.description: Existing llm/request/v1 and llm/response/v1 requests, providers, response statuses, and tests remain compatible.
items.reason: The new capability must not silently break current structured-completion consumers.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The existing test suite passes and v1 request/response schema validation remains unchanged.

items.name: declare-tools
items.description: A v2 request can declare bounded named tools with descriptions and JSON input schemas, plus autoInvokeTools and a bounded tool-round limit.
items.reason: The model must receive an explicit available-tool contract.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Duplicate names, invalid tool schemas, invalid bounds, and auto-invocation without an invoker fail before provider invocation.

items.name: parallel-tool-call-batches
items.description: The public complete tool_calls array contains ordered parallel tool call batches; calls within a batch may run concurrently and batches run sequentially.
items.reason: The contract must reinforce parallel invocation while preserving dependencies between batches.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The schemas and tests use the term parallel tool call batch, preserve input order, and prove inner parallelism with outer sequential ordering.

items.name: validate-before-invoke
items.description: Every provider-returned tool-call response is fully validated, including the tool-round budget, before any tool call is executed.
items.reason: A round-limit violation must never partially execute a model response.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the returned tool_calls structure exceeds the configured tool-round limit, the response is unvalidated, no tool invoker call occurs, and the result identifies the limit violation.

items.name: manual-and-auto-modes
items.description: autoInvokeTools false returns validated pending tool calls without executing them; autoInvokeTools true executes only validated calls through the injected invoker and continues bounded model rounds.
items.reason: Callers need both approval/manual orchestration and bounded automatic orchestration modes.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Manual mode returns tool_calls_pending and automatic mode returns terminal success, tool-round exhaustion, or sanitized invocation failure according to the bounded lifecycle.

items.name: openrouter-transport
items.description: The OpenRouter adapter maps tool definitions and tool results to provider-native messages and normalizes native tool calls without exposing provider wire details to callers.
items.reason: The built-in provider must support the public contract.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Mocked fetch tests verify declarations, tool calls, tool results, malformed arguments, and credentials without a live request.

items.name: bounded-safe-evidence
items.description: Tool invocation is bounded, abortable, sanitized, and covered by deterministic tests, schema validation, typecheck, build, and provider-free CLI checks.
items.reason: A tool-capable library must not become an unbounded agent or leak sensitive data.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The final evidence records passing tests and explicit non-claims for live provider, production, deployment, and downstream integration behavior.
